log.title: Initial squad built
log.summary: All 599 players fed through the projection model, then optimised under the real constraints: £100.0m, 2/5/5/3, max 3 per club. Landed on a 4-4-2 spending exactly £100.0m.
evidence: Haaland and João Pedro included partly on ownership — at 69% and 63%, not owning them is the biggest single risk in the game.
Gabriel is the highest-projected defender: 9.1 CBIT/90 gives a 42% chance of the defensive bonus every week, on top of a 49% clean-sheet probability.
Wieffer, Damsgaard and Sessegnon are sub-1% owned but hit their defensive thresholds 82%, 37% and 64% of the time — the market has not priced defensive contribution properly.

log.title: Foden → Enzo Fernández
log.summary: Swapped before submitting. Same £7.0m price. Foden projected slightly higher per 90 but appeared in only 51% of predicted Man City XIs.
evidence: Foden: 2,078 minutes last season, 51% of predicted starting XIs — effectively a coin flip.
Enzo: 3,114 minutes, 87% of predicted XIs, on Chelsea set pieces and second penalties.
Also reduced Man City exposure from three players to two, cutting rotation risk concentration.

log.title: Verified against press conferences
log.summary: Every one of the fifteen cross-checked against manager press conferences and predicted lineups before submitting.
evidence: Arteta confirmed Saliba is a long-term absence and Timber is not yet training — strengthens Gabriel and Calafiori rather than threatening them.
Le Bris: all Sunderland players available except Adingra. Ballard clear.
Doku ruled out for Man City, which is what opens the number-ten role for Cherki (66% of predicted XIs).
Sessegnon absent from Fulham's predicted XI — flagged as a risk, but he is bench slot 3 so the cost this week is near zero.

glossary.plain: How many goals a player would be expected to score from the shots he's taken, based on how good those chances were. A high xG means he's getting into good scoring positions, even on games he doesn't actually score.
The same idea, for the passes leading to a shot — how many assists you'd expect from the quality of chances he's created.
The estimated chance a team doesn't concede a goal in a match. Goalkeepers and defenders get 4 points for a clean sheet, midfielders get 1.

A newer way to score points for defensive work — tackles, interceptions, blocks, ball recoveries. Hit a threshold in a game (10 for defenders, 12 for midfielders/forwards) and you earn 2 points, even without a goal or clean sheet.

A 1–5 rating of how hard a team's next opponent is expected to be — 1–2 is a kind fixture, 4–5 is a tough one. Used to weight the projections toward players facing weaker defences (or weaker attacks, for defenders).
The top 3 performers in each match, as scored by the official Bonus Points System, get 3, 2 and 1 extra points. Estimated here from a player's BPS rate.

The percentage of all Fantasy managers who currently own a player. A high-ownership player who scores big doesn't gain you much rank; a low-ownership player who scores big gains you a lot — and costs you a lot if he doesn't play.
This model's estimate of a player's points for a single gameweek, built from all of the above and blended with his actual scoring record.
